---
title: "Bookmarks"
---

Hover any heading on this page and a star appears in its left margin. Click it to bookmark
that section. Bookmarked sections keep a persistent star, and the reader menu gathers them
into a Bookmarks list you can jump between or clear.

## Why sections, not paragraphs

A bookmark answers "take me back to the part about X". The natural unit of "a part" is a
section, so the gesture lives on headings rather than on arbitrary text. Highlights already
cover marking a single passage; bookmarks are the lighter, coarser sibling.

## Anchored to the block, not the text

Each bookmark stores the heading's content-hash block id, not a fuzzy text match, so it is
exact and survives a re-render or a layout change. Editing a heading's text away orphans its
bookmark gracefully: the id stops resolving and the entry is simply skipped, never
mis-placed onto the wrong section.

## Kept by the reader, carried by no server

Bookmarks live in the reader's own browser storage, keyed by the page path. Nothing is sent
anywhere; the document stays read-only and authoritative while each reader keeps a private
set of places worth returning to.

## A longer document earns it

On a short page a bookmark is a convenience. In a book chapter, where the sections you care
about are scattered across a long scroll, a gathered list of them is the difference between
returning in one click and hunting by eye.
